FLAG ON CSV TOWN: the temple is at Nartiang village in West Jaintia Hills district, NOT Jowai (Jowai is the district headquarters town, approx. 25 km away) - the CSV town is wrong. Nartiang was the summer capital of the Jaintia Kingdom; its Durga temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas (Shakti as 'Jayanti', Bhairava as 'Kamadishwar'), believed to mark where Sati's left thigh fell, and the goddess is locally known as Jainteshwari. King Jaso Manik (1606-1641) married Lakshmi Narayana, daughter of Koch king Nara Narayana, whose influence is credited with bringing Shaktism to the Jaintia royalty; legend says the goddess appeared to Jaso Manik in a dream and asked him to build the temple. Worship blends Hindu and Khasi-Jaintia traditions - the deity is a decorated plantain trunk, not an idol - and the local Syiem remains the chief patron; the present priests are direct descendants of the original priests from Jaintiapur. Ancient cannons of the Jaintia kings are kept on the premises. The Central Puja Committee of Meghalaya maintains the temple; in 2017 the Union government announced it would be declared a heritage site (verify current status).

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
town_description: Nartiang is a historic village in West Jaintia Hills district, about 60-65 km east of Shillong on the Shillong-Jowai road. Once the summer capital of the Jaintia Kingdom, it is famous as the 'Garden of Monoliths' - scattered clusters of ancient Khasi-Jaintia menhirs and dolmens - and for the Nartiang Durga Temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Nearby attractions include Thadlaskein Lake and the district town of Jowai (~25 km).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Durga Puja (September-October) is the most significant and vibrant time to visit, though crowded with pilgrims from across the Northeast.
